newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt to get chance to appoint High Court judge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt to get chance to appoint High Court judge.

text.p: The government of Prime Minister John Howard will get its first chance to appoint a judge to the nation's peak court after judge Daryl Dawson announced his resignation on Wednesday.
A spokesman for Dawson said the 63-year-old judge would quit the High Court in August after 15 years on the seven-member bench.
Critics claim the court is dominated by progressive judges, appointed under the 13-year Labor government which was ousted last year, and favours flexible interpretations of the law in its judgments.

Some leading conservative politicians have urged reform of the court and tighter controls on its operations after recent controversial decisions, including the December Wik judgment recognising Aboriginal land rights on pastoral land.
High Court judges must retire at 70 but Dawson was resigning early to spend more time with his family, the spokesman said.
A second court vacancy will open when chief judge Gerard Brennan retires next year, when he turns 70.
Dawson's spokesman said the judge had no major cases scheduled before his retirement.
